Cash-flow and pricing vocabulary

After this lesson you can:
  • Distinguish principal, interest, fee and charge
  • Compare reducing, flat, fixed and floating rate
  • Read APR and schedule terms correctly

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. Four different money concepts
  2. Rate language
  3. Schedule language
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS
  6. Knowledge check

1. Four different money concepts

Principal is funded and outstanding capital.

Interest is time-based consideration on the defined balance.

A fee pays for a service or event.

A charge responds to a condition or breach.

Tax is a statutory amount on the applicable fee or service.

Their disclosure, accrual, allocation and reversal rules differ.

2. Rate language

Fixed versus floating describes whether the contractual rate can reset.

Reducing versus flat describes the balance used to calculate interest.

Nominal rate is not APR.

Benchmark, spread, reset date, lookback and rounding together define a floating-rate outcome.

3. Schedule language

EMI, instalment, due, overdue, accrued, capitalised and paid are not synonyms.

Bullet, balloon, step-up, seasonal, moratorium and irregular schedules alter when principal or interest is payable.

Value date controls economic placement; posting date records system entry.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-KFS-2024 — Standardised cash-flow disclosure and APR depend on precise terms.
  • RBI-FPC-PENAL — Penal charges must remain charges and cannot be capitalised.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability PRD-003 — Interest-method configuration.
  • Capability PRD-005 — APR composition.
  • Capability LMS-001 — Reducing-balance amortisation.
  • Capability LMS-004 — Structured schedules.

Retrieval practice

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. Does a fixed rate imply reducing-balance interest?

  1. Always
  2. No; reset behaviour and calculation balance are separate dimensions
  3. Only for retail loans
  4. Only when APR equals the rate
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Fixed/floating and flat/reducing describe different dimensions.
